purpose: General principles for authoring design documents (How): definition, what to omit, quantitative targets, judgment criteria, hierarchy, architecture norms, and a severity catalog for review.
summary: Definition of a design document: responsibility is structure, modules and flows (How); permanent but revisable via additive development
Prohibited content: bulk source code, unjustified framework choice, features absent from requirements, guaranteed quantitative claims
Handling of quantitative targets: describe structure and policy only, never guarantee achievement or guess unconfirmed values
Judgment criterion: can an implementer implement from this; hierarchical splitting guidance and optional sections
Mermaid diagram guidelines and a ban on history sections; maintenance rule to report design-implementation mismatches to the user
Architecture dependency direction norms, responsibility and cohesion norms (YAGNI, asset placement), availability and SPOF norms
Severity catalog mapping violations to critical, major or minor, including deliverable checks and additive feature frontmatter
tasks: Updating a design document after implementation changes
Deciding whether content belongs in design or requirements
Assigning severity to design review findings
Splitting a large design into hierarchical documents
title: 設計書 作成原則
